_comment: P0 engagement economy. Capital is engagement-scoped and integer-valued (no float money, ever - it would break determinism hashing for no benefit). Integrity is the lives pool; in P3 it becomes run-scoped Corridor Integrity and stops resetting between engagements. sell_refund_fraction is below 1 on purpose: relocating a turret should cost something, or placement stops being a decision. early_wave_bonus is paid pro rata for the slice of the inter-wave gap given up, so calling a wave in early trades preparation time for money. carry_limit_share is 1.0: every turret you built carries forward. It was 0.55 for one revision, which stopped an inherited board winning the next act unattended and did it by deleting turrets the player had paid for - reported immediately, and rightly. The same job is now done by how deeply a carried turret is refitted, which costs tiers rather than emplacements. board_salvage_fraction is what a finished board converts into when the campaign moves to a different map. Turrets cannot cross - a coordinate on one board means nothing on another - but the work can, and arriving at a new board with nothing to show for the last one reads as the game deleting your progress. Opening Capital on a board-opening act is reduced to match what a competent finish salvages, so this is continuity rather than a bonus. interest_per_wave pays a share of Capital still in hand when a wave begins, and exists to create a decision rather than to hand out money: without it, Capital not spent the instant it arrives is Capital wasted, so building now beats building better in two waves unconditionally. interest_cap bounds it, because a percentage of an unbounded pile is an unbounded pile - uncapped, the right play late in a long act becomes building nothing and banking, which is the opposite of what it was added for. support_cap_* bound what one turret can receive from every neighbour combined. Capped by TOTAL rather than by number of sources, because 'the first three contributors in index order' is deterministic and arbitrary, and a rule nobody can predict is not a rule anyone can play around.
